items.title: CMYK halftone print screens
items.summary: Reproduce colour printing: the image is split into cyan, magenta, yellow and black, each printed as dots on its own rotated grid with dot size following the ink amount, then composited on paper.
contract: unshaded, cull_disabled, depth_test_disabled, depth_draw_never, skip_vertex_transform, fog_disabled
screen_texture (sampler2D), dot_spacing (float = 7), dot_softness (float = 0.8), paper_color (vec4 = 0.97, 0.95, 0.9, 1), ink_strength (float = 1), monochrome (bool = no)
A MeshInstance3D with a 2 x 2 QuadMesh, `material.tres` as its material override and a large extra cull margin, as in `demo.tscn`.
The scene printed as overlapping cyan, magenta, yellow and black dot screens on cream paper.
compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Dots sample the ink at each pixel, not at the cell centre, so dot edges follow image edges slightly. The RGB to CMYK conversion is the naive formula without colour management. Dot spacing is in screen pixels. The pass reads Godot's screen texture after opaque geometry, so transparent objects drawn after it are not processed and its order among other transparent passes is not controlled.
techniques: CMYK separation
Rotated halftone screens at traditional angles
Dot area proportional to ink
Subtractive compositing

items.title: Woven fabric with thread relief and sheen

contract: warp_color (vec4 = 0.22, 0.32, 0.55, 1), weft_color (vec4 = 0.75, 0.72, 0.65, 1), threads (float = 60), twill (bool = yes), thread_gap (float = 0.12), relief (float = 0.6), fuzz (float = 0.25), sheen (float = 0.6)

A blue and cream twill cloth with visible rounded threads and diagonal ribs.
compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Threads alias into moire when they get smaller than a few pixels; lower `threads` for distant cloth. Relief is a normal map only. The rim sheen depends on renderer support for the RIM output.
techniques: Plain and twill weave from a cell over/under rule
Rounded thread profile as a normal map
Directional fibre noise
RIM output for cloth sheen

items.limits: The flow coordinate is continuous within a tile but its direction can reverse between tiles, so pulses do not follow a whole path consistently.

Hashed tile orientation
MurmurHash3 32-bit finalizer over prime-combined lattice coordinates as a hash

items.title: Billboard modes: spherical or upright cylindrical
items.summary: Vertex billboarding for cards with two modes: spherical (faces the camera fully, for glows and particles) or cylindrical (turns only around the world Y axis, for trees and characters that must stay upright), keeping node position and scale.
contract: card_texture (sampler2D), tint (vec4 = 1, 1, 1, 1), mode (int = 1), alpha_cutoff (float = 0.5), shade_as_upright (bool = yes)
Card textures with alpha, and quads whose origin sits at the base for cylindrical mode (the demo uses `center_offset`).
Round green tree cards standing upright and turning to face the camera as it moves.
compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Cards rotate in the vertex stage, so frustum culling and shadows use the unrotated mesh bounds; give nodes a margin. Shadow maps render the card facing the light camera, not the main camera. Cylindrical mode degenerates when the camera is exactly above the card.
techniques: Spherical billboard from the inverse view rotation
Axis-locked cylindrical billboard
Alpha cut-out with bent normals

items.title: Blueprint x-ray with dashed hidden lines
items.summary: Show a mesh as a see-through blueprint drawing: solid white contour lines on front faces, dashed lines for contours on hidden back faces, a faint object-space graph paper grid and a translucent blue fill.

compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Contour lines come from the facing ratio, so flat faces seen edge-on fill completely and creases between flat faces are not drawn. Dashes run diagonally in screen space and do not follow the curve. Not sorted against other transparent objects.
techniques: Facing ratio contours
Back-face rendering with screen-space dashes for hidden lines

items.title: Box-projected decal from the depth buffer
items.summary: Project a decal onto whatever geometry lies inside a box: the box's pixels rebuild the scene position from depth, move it into the box's local space, discard outside the box, fade on steep surfaces, and draw a procedural emblem or an assigned image.
contract: depth_texture (sampler2D), decal_texture (sampler2D), decal_color (vec4 = 0.95, 0.75, 0.1, 1), accent_color (vec4 = 0.08, 0.08, 0.08, 1), opacity (float = 0.9), angle_fade (float = 0.4), edge_fade (float = 0.05), stripe_count (int = 10) and 1 more
A unit BoxMesh node scaled and rotated to the decal volume; its local Y is the projection axis., Optional: a decal image for `decal_texture`.
A yellow and black hazard disc painted across the floor and wrapping onto the crate inside the box.
compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Projects onto every opaque surface in the box, including moving characters; filter with layers if needed. Transparent objects are not in the depth buffer. The decal does not receive lighting (unshaded). Reconstructed normals are flat per pixel quad and can flicker at depth discontinuities.
techniques: Deferred (screen-space) decal by depth reconstruction into box space
Normal from derivatives of the reconstructed position
Procedural emblem

items.title: Brushed metal with a Ward anisotropic highlight
items.summary: Brushed metal with a custom light function: a Ward anisotropic specular stretched along a brushing direction (linear along the tangent or circular around a UV centre) plus fine procedural brush streaks.
contract: metal_color (vec4 = 0.82, 0.83, 0.85, 1), roughness_along (float = 0.08), roughness_across (float = 0.45), circular (bool = no), circle_center_u (float = 0.5), circle_center_v (float = 0.5), streak_density (float = 600), streak_strength (float = 0.25) and 2 more
A mesh with UVs and tangents.
Metal with a bright highlight smeared along the brushing, here as rings across a spun disc.
compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: Ignores environment reflections: only scene lights give specular, so add a light or use Godot's built-in ANISOTROPY output when reflections matter. Ward's model is not energy conserving at grazing angles. Circular brushing needs UVs centred on the disc (the CylinderMesh caps qualify).
techniques: Ward anisotropic BRDF (Ward 1992)
Fragment-to-light varying for a per-pixel tangent frame
Value noise with quintic interpolation and fractional Brownian motion for brush streaks

items.title: Colour vision deficiency simulation
items.summary: Simulate protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia or achromatopsia on the whole screen with a severity mix, to check that a game's colours stay distinguishable for colour-blind players.
contract: unshaded, cull_disabled, depth_test_disabled, depth_draw_never, skip_vertex_transform, fog_disabled

compatibility: compiled and rendered, forward plus: not verified, mobile: not verified
items.limits: A simulation for testing, not a correction filter, and only for typical dichromacy. Individual vision varies. The pass assumes the screen texture holds sRGB-encoded colour. The pass reads Godot's screen texture after opaque geometry, so transparent objects drawn after it are not processed and its order among other transparent passes is not controlled.
techniques: Machado et al. 2009 colour vision deficiency matrices
sRGB to linear conversion
Rec. 709 luminance for achromatopsia

items.title: Depth of field with a golden-angle bokeh gather
items.summary: Blur the scene by distance from a focus plane: a circle of confusion per pixel from the depth buffer and a gather of samples on a golden-angle spiral, weighted so sharp foreground edges do not smear.

items.limits: A gather approximation: out-of-focus foreground cannot spread over in-focus objects behind it (no scatter). Alpha-tested screen-door transparency

items.limits: One still frame of a stylized spectrum, not an ocean simulation: there is no dispersion relation, time animation or FFT, and the spectrum shape is a log-normal band with cosine spreading rather than a measured model such as JONSWAP. items.limits: One radius for every edge; no per-edge radii or chamfers. No texture coordinates. The rounded bands use a lattice pulled onto the surface, so their quads are not exactly even.
techniques: Minkowski sum of a box and a sphere (nearest inner-box point plus radius)
Non-uniform lattice with quarter-circle spacing

items.title: Superellipsoid superquadric
items.summary: Generate Barr superquadric solids whose two exponents morph between boxes, cylinders, ellipsoids, diamonds and pinched stars, with the exact smooth volume available. Use it for rounded props and shape fitting.
contract: size_x, size_y, size_z, north_south, east_west, segments, rings
items.limits: Even angle sampling crowds vertices near sharp edges and leaves flat sides coarse for small exponents; exponents near 0 produce nearly degenerate thin faces. No texture coordinates. Normals are mesh normals, not the analytic surface normals.
techniques: Barr superquadric with signed powers of cosine and sine
Superellipsoid volume via beta functions

items.title: Threaded rod with a trapezoidal helical thread
items.summary: Generate a closed threaded rod whose radius follows a trapezoidal thread profile along a helix, with flat crest and root. Use it for bolts, screws, jar necks and lead screws.
contract: major_radius, minor_radius, pitch, length, crest, root, segments, samples_per_pitch
items.limits: A single right-hand start; the ends are cut flat through the thread without a chamfer. The flanks are sampled on a fixed grid, so the crest and root corners are only as sharp as the axial sampling. Dimensions are free numbers, not tied to a thread standard.
techniques: Helical radius function r(theta, y) = minor + depth * profile(y / pitch - theta / 2 pi)
Trapezoidal thread profile

items.title: Torus with wrapped texture coordinates
items.summary: Build a ring torus around the Y axis with unit normals and a texture grid that wraps in both directions. Use it for rings, donuts, tyres and as a genus-one test surface.
items.limits: The texture seam duplicates one row and one column, so the mesh is closed only after welding. Self-intersecting (horn and spindle) tori, with the minor radius at or above the major radius, are not handled specially. The polygon volume is below the smooth torus's.
techniques: Torus parameterization ((R + r cos v) cos u, r sin v, -(R + r cos v) sin u)
Polygonal surface of revolution

items.title: UV sphere with texture seam and pole fans
items.summary: Build a latitude and longitude sphere with unit normals, a texture seam and one pole vertex per segment. Use it for globes, planets and any sphere that takes an equirectangular texture.
items.limits: The seam and the pole vertices are duplicated for texture coordinates, so the mesh is closed only after welding coincident vertices. Pole triangles are thin and the faces are not equal in area; use an icosphere or a cube sphere for even tessellation. The polygon volume and area are below the true sphere's and approach them as segments and rings grow.
techniques: Spherical coordinates (polar angle, longitude)
Equirectangular texture mapping

items.title: Wireframe overlay material
items.summary: Build a material that renders every polygon edge as a glowing line over a base surface, with the line width in pixels or metres and an optional fade on surfaces seen edge-on. Use it for technical renders, topology presentations, sci-fi looks and blueprint styles.
contract: material_name, line_color, surface_color, line_width, use_pixel_size, line_strength, fade_grazing, assign
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Relies on the Wireframe shader node, which Cycles renders; EEVEE does not support it and shows the base surface only. Edges come from the triangulated render mesh, so n-gons show their internal triangulation. Lines are emissive and do not cast shadows. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Wireframe shader node in pixel or world size
Facing term to fade lines at grazing angles
Mix of a surface and an emission

items.title: Physical sky with a matching sun lamp
items.summary: Build a physical sky world and a sun lamp whose direction matches the sky's sun exactly, from one elevation and compass bearing, with the sky's sun disc off so the lamp gives sharp direct light. Use it for exteriors, architecture and time-of-day studies.
contract: elevation, azimuth, sun_strength, sun_angle, world_strength, sky_sun_disc, air_density, haze
A world named Baltor Sky set as the scene world, and a sun lamp named Baltor Sky Sun.
items.limits: The bearing convention (clockwise from +Y, as the Sky Texture sun rotation) was measured on Blender 5.2.1 only. Uses the multiple scattering sky where Blender offers it and the Nishita sky otherwise; their colours differ. Lamp strength is a free parameter, not derived from the sky model, so sky and sun brightness are balanced by eye. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Sun direction from elevation and bearing on the unit sphere
Light rotation that points a lamp's -Z axis along a direction
Equirectangular panorama render used to measure the sky's sun convention

items.title: Helical compression spring with spring rate
items.summary: Generate a compression spring as a round wire swept along a helix with closed end coils, and report its free length, solid length and spring rate from the wire material. Use it for mechanisms, suspension props and machine details.
contract: mean_diameter, wire_diameter, active_coils, pitch, end_coils, clockwise, samples_per_turn, wire_sides and 1 more
One closed, smooth-shaded mesh object named Coil Spring along +Z.
items.limits: Ends are closed but not ground flat, so the spring does not stand on a flat face. The height changes pitch abruptly where active coils meet end coils. The rate uses the basic formula G d^4 / (8 D^3 n) without the Wahl curvature correction and assumes small deflections. Extension spring hooks are not modelled. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Helix sweep in the radial and tangent frame without twist
Piecewise pitch for closed end coils
Helical spring rate k = G d^4 / (8 D^3 n)

items.title: Three-point light rig with illuminance ratios
items.summary: Add key, fill and rim area lights aimed at a target, placed by azimuth and elevation, with fill and rim powers derived from illuminance ratios at their distances. Use it to light a subject for product, character or turntable renders.
contract: target, key_distance, fill_distance, rim_distance, key_azimuth, key_elevation, fill_azimuth, fill_elevation and 9 more
An empty with three parented area lights constrained to aim at it.
items.limits: Powers follow the inverse square law from each light's centre, which is approximate for area lights that are large compared with their distance. The ratios hold at the target point only. Colours are linear RGB values, not colour temperatures. The lights stay aimed by Track To constraints on the rig empty; glTF export keeps their positions but not the constraints. Verified in Blender 5.2.1 with Cycles; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Three-point lighting: key, fill and rim (back) light
Inverse square law to hold illuminance ratios across distances
Spherical coordinates for light placement
Euler XYZ angles that point the -Z axis along a direction

items.title: Barrel from bulged staves, hoops and heads
items.summary: Generate a cooper-style barrel: separate bulged staves with gaps, iron hoops that follow the bilge and recessed head discs, each a closed solid with its own material slot, plus the outer volume in litres. Use it for taverns, cellars, ships and game props.
contract: height, head_radius, bilge_radius, staves, stave_thickness, gap, rows, hoops and 2 more
One mesh object named Barrel with stave, hoop and head material slots.
items.limits: The bilge is a parabola in height, not a measured cooperage curve. Staves are faceted (one chord per stave across its width) and have no bevel, chime chamfer or bung hole. Hoops are plain rectangular bands with no rivets. The volume is the outer volume from the profile, not the inner capacity. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Parabolic bilge profile r(z) = r_head + (r_bilge - r_head)(1 - (2z/H - 1)^2)
Closed slabs from a two-sided grid with side walls
Rectangular-section rings as closed genus-one solids

items.title: Batch rename objects by rule
items.summary: Rename many objects at once by rule: strip .001 suffixes, find and replace with optional regular expressions, apply a case style, add a prefix and suffix, and number only the names that would collide. Use it to prepare scenes for export and naming conventions.
contract: prefix, suffix, find, replace, use_regex, case, strip_duplicate_suffix, numbering and 5 more
Objects renamed in place; the plan is returned as a report.
items.limits: Renames objects and, when they have a single user, their data; materials, collections and other data blocks keep their names. Case splitting is a heuristic for ASCII words and digit runs. Names are cut to 63 bytes, so very long names lose their end. Regular expressions use Python syntax. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Two-pass renaming through temporary names to avoid automatic .001 suffixes
Word splitting at case changes and digit runs with regular expressions
Collision-free numbering within groups of equal names

items.title: Bounce animation with exact parabolic arcs
items.summary: Key a bouncing motion on the active object from drop height, restitution and gravity: exact parabolic arcs, decaying rebounds, constant travel and optional squash at contacts. Use it for balls, props and motion tests.
contract: drop_height, ground_z, radius, measure_radius, restitution, gravity, fps, start_frame and 4 more
Keyframes on the active object: location Z with free handles, location X linear, scale squash keys.
items.limits: Point-mass free fall with a constant restitution: no air drag, spin, rolling or deformation physics. The squash is a stylized scale key at each contact, scaled with impact speed, and it lowers the contact key by radius times squash so the object stays on the ground. Motion is along +X on a flat ground only. Keys sit on fractional frames. Verified in Blender 5.2.1, where F-curves live in the action's channel bag; the 4.2 code path uses action.fcurves and was not run.
techniques: Free fall: t = sqrt(2 h / g), apex height times restitution squared per bounce
Degree elevation of a quadratic Bezier to a cubic: handles at one third of the span
Cubic Bezier F-curve evaluation by solving for the curve parameter
Volume-preserving squash: scale z by 1 - s and x, y by 1 / sqrt(1 - s)

items.title: Brick wall in English, Flemish and other bonds
items.summary: Generate a brick wall course by course in stretcher, stack, English, Flemish or common bond, with mortar joints, cut bricks at the ends, queen closers and seeded colour variation. Use it for architecture, ruins and game environments that need real brick geometry.
contract: bond, length, courses, brick, joint, header_every, recess, seed
One mesh object named Brick Wall with four material slots.
items.limits: Straight walls only; no openings, corners that interlock with a return wall, arches or chamfers. Bricks are sharp boxes without bevels. The mortar is a recessed core box, not tooled joint profiles. Brick sizes default to UK metric bricks; set others with the brick parameter. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Masonry bonds: stretcher, stack, English, Flemish and common (American)
Queen closer to offset header courses by a quarter brick
Seeded integer hash to assign material slots

items.title: Cast concrete material with pores and board seams
items.summary: Build a concrete node material with water stains, aggregate specks from Voronoi cells, darkened and recessed air pores, and optional seams from board formwork every board width. Use it for brutalist architecture, floors, bunkers and urban scenes.
contract: material_name, color, stain_strength, aggregate_scale, aggregate_amount, pore_scale, pore_depth, board_lines and 2 more
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Pores and aggregate come from Voronoi cells, which are evenly spread rather than graded like real aggregate. Board seams are horizontal only (along object Z) and carry no wood grain imprint. No cracks or spalling. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Voronoi F1 distance thresholds for specks and pores
Low-frequency noise through a colour ramp for stains
Periodic seams from the fractional part of height over board width

items.title: Catenary cable between two points
items.summary: Hang a cable between two anchor points as an exact catenary for a given slack, swept as a round tube, and report the sag, the lowest point and the tension ratio at the anchors. Use it for power lines, ropes, hoses and hanging wires.
contract: start, end, slack, radius, segments, sides
One smooth-shaded closed mesh named Catenary Cable in world coordinates.
items.limits: A uniform, perfectly flexible and inextensible cable under gravity only: no wind, stiffness, stretch or point loads. The anchors must differ horizontally; a vertical hang is refused. Very large slack values make a deep U that the segment count may sample coarsely. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Catenary y = a cosh((x - x0) / a) + c through two points with a given arc length
Bisection on the monotone function 2 a sinh(h / (2 a))
Parallel transport of a section frame along a sampled curve

items.title: Cavity dirt material with vertical streaks
items.summary: Build a grime node material where dirt collects in crevices found by ambient occlusion and runs down in vertical streaks from a noise stretched along Z, darkening and roughening a base colour. Use it for buildings, statues, machinery and props that need dirt in the right places.
contract: material_name, base_color, dirt_color, ao_distance, dirt_amount, streaks, streak_scale, assign
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Cavities come from the Ambient Occlusion shader node: ray traced in Cycles, screen-space approximated in EEVEE, so results differ. Streaks follow object Z and do not know about ledges or drip sources. Dirt is colour and roughness only, without bump. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Ambient occlusion as a cavity mask (1 - AO)
Anisotropic noise by scaling one axis of the coordinates
Soft threshold by map range

items.title: Displaced icosphere rock with fractured facets
items.summary: Generate a closed rock mesh from a seed: an icosphere displaced by fractal value noise, sheared by random planes into flat facets and flattened at the base. Use it for props, scatter sources and level dressing.
contract: seed, subdivisions, radius, dimensions, roughness, frequency, octaves, cuts and 3 more
One closed mesh object named Rock with a UVMap and one material slot.
items.limits: Displacement is radial, so overhangs and deep cracks cannot form. The noise is value noise on an integer lattice, which shows mild grid alignment at low octave counts. Strong cuts or a high flat base can produce long thin triangles. One material slot with a flat colour; no texture or weathering. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Icosphere by recursive four-way triangle subdivision projected to the sphere
Value noise with quintic fade and integer hash lattice, fractal sum of octaves
Planar cuts by projecting points beyond a half-space onto its plane
Spherical UV mapping with seam correction per face

items.title: Edge wear material from the Bevel node
items.summary: Build a painted-metal node material that wears through to bare metal along convex edges: the Bevel node normal is compared with the true normal, and the edge term is broken up by noise into chips. Use it for tools, vehicles, props and game assets that need handled edges.
contract: material_name, paint_color, metal_color, wear_width, sensitivity, wear_amount, noise_scale, assign
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Relies on the Bevel shader node, which only Cycles evaluates; EEVEE returns the plain normal, so no wear appears there. Detects convex and concave edges alike within the radius. Noise-based chips, not a wear simulation. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Bevel shader normal versus true normal as an edge detector
Noise-modulated threshold for chipped wear
Mix shader between paint and metal

items.title: Fractal noise terrain with islands, ridges and terraces
items.summary: Generate a grid terrain from fractal gradient noise with ridged mode, island falloff, terraces, sea-level flattening and an optional closed base, plus a vertex group for the sea floor. Use it for landscapes, game maps, dioramas and printable relief models.
contract: size, resolution, height, feature_size, octaves, lacunarity, gain, ridged and 5 more
One smooth-shaded mesh object named Terrain with a UVMap and a sea vertex group.
items.limits: A height field: no caves, overhangs or erosion simulation. Gradient noise on a square lattice can show faint axis alignment. Terraces use a quartic softened step and island falloff a radial smoothstep, both stylized rather than geological. High resolutions are slow in pure Python (1024 cells per side is about a million vertices). Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Gradient (Perlin-style) noise with hashed gradients and quintic fade
Fractal Brownian motion with lacunarity and gain
Ridged multifractal fold 1 - |n|
Radial smoothstep island falloff

items.title: Geodesic dome with strut length classes
items.summary: Generate a geodesic dome of any frequency from a vertex-up icosahedron, as hexagonal struts with hubs or as a closed panel shell, and list the distinct strut lengths with counts and chord factors. Use it for domes, greenhouses, sci-fi habitats and build planning.
contract: frequency, radius, mode, strut_radius, hub_radius, thickness
One mesh object named Geodesic Dome standing on z = 0.
items.limits: Class I subdivision with the vertex-up orientation only; other classes, orientations and truncations (such as 5/8 domes) are not available. Odd frequencies end in a stepped rim. Struts are straight hexagonal prisms that overlap the hubs; connector design, panel joints and loads are not modelled. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Class I geodesic subdivision of icosahedron faces into a triangular grid
Projection of grid points onto the sphere
Chord factors of geodesic struts
Hemisphere cut along the equator of a vertex-up icosahedron

items.title: Glazed ceramic tile material with bevelled edges
items.summary: Build a square tile node material from math nodes: grout lines, rounded tile edges by bump, a glossy glaze whose colour varies per tile from a cell hash, and rough grout. Use it for kitchens, bathrooms, pools and floors.
contract: material_name, orientation, tile_size, grout_width, bevel, glaze_a, glaze_b, grout_color and 2 more
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Square grid tiles only; no offset, herringbone or hexagonal layouts (see the tiled floor generator for geometry layouts). The bevel is a bump effect, not geometry. Colour variation is a mix of two glaze colours per tile, not crackle or pooling. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Cell index by floor and in-cell position by fraction of scaled coordinates
Distance to the nearest square edge: 0.5 - max(|x - 0.5|, |y - 0.5|)
Per-cell random values from white noise of the cell index

items.title: HDRI environment world with a solid camera backdrop
items.summary: Build an image-based lighting world from an equirectangular image with rotation, strength and saturation, and optionally show the camera a solid colour while the image still lights the scene and fills reflections. Use it for product shots, look development and outdoor lighting.
contract: image_path, rotation, strength, saturation, backdrop, backdrop_color
A world named Baltor HDRI with the image loaded, set as the scene world.
items.limits: Needs an image file; the demo fixture writes a small 8-bit PNG sky, which lights only roughly because it holds no high dynamic range. No ground projection, sun extraction or importance map tuning. The solid backdrop uses the Light Path node, which Cycles honours fully and EEVEE only partly. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Equirectangular environment lookup with a Z rotation
Light Path camera ray mask to separate backdrop from lighting
Hue Saturation adjustment of an environment

items.title: Height fog volume with exponential falloff
items.summary: Add a box of volumetric fog whose density falls off exponentially with height above its base and drifts in noise patches, with scattering colour and anisotropy, shown as bounds in the viewport. Use it for morning mist, valleys, dungeons and atmospheric depth.
contract: size, density, falloff, breakup, noise_scale, color, anisotropy
A box mesh named Height Fog with the volume material Baltor Height Fog.
items.limits: Volumetric rendering is slow and noisy at low sample counts; EEVEE renders volumes with its own approximations. The fog fills only its box, so its edges show if the box is smaller than the view. Density follows the box's own base height from its origin, not the scene floor. The visibility in the report is the rough 3 / density rule for a dense medium. Verified in Blender 5.2.1 with Cycles CPU; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Exponential height fog d0 exp(-(z - base) / h)
Principled Volume with Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy
Noise breakup of density

items.title: Hologram material with scanlines and glitch bands
items.summary: Build a see-through hologram material: thin glowing scanlines from world height, a bright Fresnel rim and noisy horizontal glitch bands, used both as emission strength and as the mix toward a transparent shader. Use it for sci-fi interfaces, projections and ghostly effects.
contract: material_name, color, line_density, line_width, rim, glitch, brightness, assign
One transparent emissive material; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Static: scanlines and glitches do not move unless you animate the mapping or a value. Lines follow world Z, so they stay horizontal when the object rotates. Transparency through a Transparent BSDF costs extra samples; EEVEE needs blended or dithered render settings. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Scanlines from the fractional part of height times density
Fresnel rim from the Layer Weight node
Thresholded noise along one axis for bands

items.title: Involute spur gear
items.summary: Generate a spur gear with true involute tooth flanks from module, tooth count and pressure angle, with backlash, face width and an optional bore, and report its pitch, tip, root and base diameters. Use it for mechanisms, gear trains and machine props that must mesh.
contract: teeth, module, pressure_angle, face_width, bore_diameter, backlash, flank_samples, smooth_bore_sides
One closed mesh object named Spur Gear, axis along Z, centred on the origin.
items.limits: Standard full-depth teeth only (addendum one module, dedendum 1.25 modules); no profile shift, no undercut or trochoid root fillet, so gears below about 17 teeth at 20 degrees are not exact near the root. The root between teeth is a straight chord, not an arc. No helix, hub or keyway. Fine for rendering and animation; check tolerances before manufacturing. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Involute of a circle and the involute function inv(a) = tan(a) - a
Tooth thickness of half the circular pitch on the pitch circle
Annulus triangulation by merging two angle-sorted loops

items.title: L-shaped stairs with a landing or winders
items.summary: Generate quarter-turn stairs: two straight flights joined by a square landing or by three winder treads cut at 30 degree steps from the inner corner, turning left or right, with an optional support block. Use it where a stair must turn a corner.
contract: first_steps, second_steps, corner, turn, rise, going, width, tread_thickness and 1 more
One mesh object named L-Shaped Stairs made of closed treads.
items.limits: Winders radiate from the inner corner, so their inner ends are very narrow; real stairs often offset the pivot to keep a minimum inner tread, which this generator does not do. No stringers, risers or handrail. Parts are separate closed solids in one mesh. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Quarter-turn stair with three winders at 30 degree increments
Ray and square intersection for winder outlines
Mirroring a mesh with reversed face winding

items.title: Lathe a profile into a solid or a hollow shell
items.summary: Revolve a list of radius and height points around Z into a solid of revolution, with poles on the axis, Chaikin rounding, partial sweeps and an optional wall thickness that turns an outline into a closed hollow vessel. Use it for vases, bottles, cups, lamps and turned parts.
contract: profile, segments, thickness, rounding, angle, smooth
One closed mesh object named Lathe with a UVMap, axis along Z.
items.limits: The shell offset moves each profile point along its averaged normal, so very sharp inner corners or walls thicker than the local curvature allows can fold; such outlines are refused only when the offset crosses the axis. A shell needs a full sweep and an open top. UVs are cylindrical and stretch near the poles. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Surface of revolution with single pole vertices on the axis
Chaikin corner cutting for open polylines
Profile offset along averaged vertex normals to build a wall

items.title: Metal materials from a reflectance table
items.summary: Build a fully metallic Principled material for gold, silver, copper, aluminium, iron, titanium, chromium, nickel, platinum, zinc, brass or cobalt from a table of approximate normal-incidence reflectance values, with roughness variation and optional brushing. Use it for jewellery, hardware and props.
contract: One metallic material named Baltor and the metal name; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: The F0 values are approximate linear sRGB reflectances rounded to two decimals; the edge tint of real metals is left to the Principled BSDF's default model, and oxidation, patina and scratches are not included. Brass and similar alloys vary with composition. Brushed anisotropy needs tangents that follow the brushing direction. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Normal-incidence reflectance (F0) as the base colour of a metallic BSDF
Approximate F0 values derived from measured complex refractive indices
Anisotropic specular for brushed metal

items.title: Metallic flake car paint with a flip colour
items.summary: Build a car paint node material: a two-tone colour that flips at grazing angles, Voronoi metal flakes that tilt the base layer's normal so they sparkle, and a smooth clear coat on its own normal. Use it for vehicles, product renders and toys.
contract: material_name, base_color, flip_color, metallic, base_roughness, flake_scale, flake_strength, coat_roughness and 1 more
One material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Flakes come from Voronoi cells in object space, so their size scales with the object and they alias at a distance unless enough samples are rendered. The flip colour uses a facing ramp, not measured pearlescent data, and the paint is not physically based beyond the Principled BSDF. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Layer Weight facing term driving a colour ramp for a flip colour
Normal perturbation by random Voronoi cell colours for flakes
Separate coat normal over a perturbed base normal

items.title: Neon tube material with a glass sheath
items.summary: Build a neon sign material: an emissive gas core, whitened at the face-on centre, mixed by the Fresnel term with a clear glass sheath that takes over toward the silhouette. Use it for signs, cyberpunk scenes, bars and stylized lighting.
contract: material_name, color, strength, core_whiteness, sheath, assign
One emissive material with a node tree; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Emission lights the scene only in renderers that treat emissive meshes as lights (Cycles does, with noise); EEVEE needs light probes or extra lamps. No bloom: add glare in the compositor. The white core is a stylized ramp, not a gas discharge spectrum. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Layer Weight facing and Fresnel terms
Mix of emission and glass by Fresnel
Colour ramp toward white for an overexposed core

items.title: Parametric table with tapered, round or turned legs
items.summary: Generate a table from overall size: a top with rounded corners, four inset legs in tapered, round or turned style, and aprons under the top, each a closed solid. Use it for interiors, product scenes and furniture blockouts.
contract: length, width, height, top_thickness, corner_radius, leg_style, leg_size, leg_inset and 2 more
One mesh object named Table standing on z = 0.
items.limits: Four-legged rectangular tables only; no pedestal, drawers, stretchers or joinery detail. Turned legs use one fixed bead profile scaled to the leg size. Parts touch but are not merged, and edges are sharp without bevels. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: Rounded rectangle from quarter-circle corners
Lofting closed solids through rings of equal vertex count
Square ring with matching vertex count by projecting angles onto the square

items.title: PBR material from a folder of maps
items.summary: Build a full PBR material from a folder of texture maps by recognising each file from the words in its name: base colour, roughness or gloss, metallic, normal (OpenGL or DirectX), height, ambient occlusion, opacity and emission, with the right colour spaces. Use it to import texture sets fast.
contract: material_name, folder, uv_scale, normal_strength, displacement_scale, ao_strength, assign
One material with image nodes; assigned to the active object.
items.limits: Recognition is by file name tokens only; files with unusual names are listed as ignored, and when two files match one channel the first in sorted order wins and the rest are reported. Packed channel maps (such as ORM) and UDIM tile sets are not split. Height goes through the Displacement node, which renders as bump unless the material's displacement method is changed. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
techniques: File name tokenisation with camel case and separator splitting
Colour space by channel: sRGB for colour, Non-Color for data maps

Signals and methods named by connections are not checked. Nodes inside instanced scenes are found by parsing those scenes (eight levels deep at most). Godot 3 scenes (format 2) are parsed with a warning, because Godot 4.7 converts their class names on load.
techniques: Godot 4 text scene and resource format: sections, header attributes, multi-line values
